endorsements.quote: AI tools must not direct, override, or simulate clinical decision-making.
Carers and clinicians must be able to query, correct, and override AI outputs without friction.
A safety prompt layer does not direct professional judgement.

unlisted_practices: Clearly identify AI-generated summaries as AI-generated.
Make the source records from which AI summaries are derived accessible to users.
Ensure every team member receiving AI-generated content understands its basis and limitations.
Test voice-based AI tools for performance equity across accent and language diversity before deployment.
Apply data minimisation, encryption, strict role-based access control, and GDPR-aligned governance to AI handover tools.
Conduct privacy impact assessments before deploying AI tools in any new care context.
Align AI handover tools with CQC fundamental standards, the NICE Evidence Standards Framework for Digital Health Technologies, and the Domiciliary AI Governance Framework.
Include mandatory confirmation mechanisms for safety-critical actions in AI handover tools.
Generate immutable audit trails for AI handover tools.
Require adoption monitoring as a contractual requirement for AI handover tools.
Involve frontline professionals in the structured co-design of AI handover tools before deployment.
Design AI handover tools to reduce administrative burden and generate compliance records automatically.

screen.reason: The paper presents a conceptual analysis and framework proposing human-centred AI design and governance requirements for clinical handovers, informed by a needs assessment survey.
